title: customer-requests-contrarian-notes-and-probe-stubs
summary: Working synthesis of recent field captured asks (June–July 2026) framed against implementation risk and unit-cost impact. Purpose: give eng/product a set of low-risk micro-probes and a couple of contrarian hypotheses where deprioritizing the obvious ask may reduce overall cost-to-serve and preserve SLOs.
key_insights: 1) Many customers ask for per-request model pinning + fallback, but the primary driver is predictable latency more than model fidelity. 2) A surprising slice of mid-market customers prefer predictable per-token cost over latest-model quality. 3) KV-cache misconfiguration is the top source of jitter reports — often a docs/usability gap, not a runtime bug. 4) Small UX changes (explicit billing classifier labels) reduce support load more than small latency wins.
prioritized_requests: Per-route fallback policy UI: allow app teams to choose fallback depth (seconds) and model tier instead of binary fallback — estimated engineering: M; business impact: high for Dedicated customers
Transparent per-token cost preview in console for planned prompts (rough token estimator view) — effort: S; impact: reduces support and churn
KV-cache diagnostic mode that surfaces prefix hit-rates per-request and suggested TTLs — effort: M; impact: high on latency variability complaints
Batching opt-in toggle per-route with suggested batch sizes based on observed request qps — effort: M; risk: medium (regression tests required)
micro_probes: Probe A: KV-cache onboarding checklist — ship checklist in docs + console tooltip + in-product checklist. Success metric: 40% reduction in 'jitter' tickets for customers with >10k qps within 30 days
Probe B: Cost-preview beta — add token-estimate button in Console for sample prompts. Run with 10 pilot accounts. Success metric: reduce billing support volume for pilots by 30%
Probe C: Fallback depth selector A/B — expose 3 presets (aggressive, balanced, conservative) to 50 customers and measure 7-day error rate and P95 latency. Success metric: fewer manual rollbacks

Probe D: Lightweight per-route tracing sample (captures model variant, batch-size, cache-hit) — enable for 5% of traffic on Dedicated nodes for two weeks. Success metric: identify top 3 misconfig patterns
raw_quotes: "We just need it to be fast and cheap — the model differences are small for us, but the latency spikes kill the UX." — B2B search product lead
"Your console says 'estimated cost' but that's a lie when we have bursts. Need a real preview." — growth PM at a startup
"We got a support ticket asking how to set TTLs for the kv-cache — doc links didn't help them." — CS agent
engineering_notes: Observations for serving/runtime team: (a) Implementing k-v cache diagnostic surface is mostly read-path instrumentation; add sample-based tracing and a simple aggregation pipeline. (b) Fallback presets should map to existing routing policy rules; add metrics instrumentation on decision latency. (c) Batching toggle must be conservative: ensure we have a non-invasive path that will not change token ordering; add e2e test that validates streaming behavior when batching changes. (d) Consider adding a cost-forecast lambda that runs in the console using current batching/cache settings to produce preview estimates.
cost_estimates: Rough engineering LOE: KV-diagnostics (2 sprints backend + 1 sprint console), Cost-preview (1 sprint console + small estimator lib), Fallback presets (1 sprint infra + 1 sprint console), Batching toggle (2 sprints safe rollout). Approx customer impact to unit-cost: KV-diagnostics -> lowers variability (qualitative), Batching toggle -> potential 10–30% token cost reduction in high-qps workloads if adopted; fallback presets -> reduces cost from emergency overprovisioning.
risks_and_open_questions: - Risk: Batching toggles can subtly change latency distributions; need canary rollout. - Question: Do we expose cost previews only in Console or also via API/SDK? - Risk: KV-diagnostics must not add significant write amplification to metrics pipeline. - Question: Which tier of customers get early access? Suggest Dedicated first.
measurement_plan: Instrument P95/P99 latency, error rate, per-route cost/unit, and support ticket volume. For each probe, set a 30-day baseline then measure delta. Use CS to label customer cohorts for pilot. Add flags to track adoption and rollback events.
next_steps: Sync with runtime squad on feasibility and e2e test plan (assign ENG-5471)
Create Confluence spec for KV-diagnostics and cost-preview with mockups (owner: Amira)
Seed a pilot cohort of 10 Dedicated customers for fallback presets (CS to coordinate)
Add a small doc rewrite for KV-cache onboarding and create console tooltips
acceptance_criteria: For each probe: clear success metric, observed delta against baseline over 30 days, and no degradation in production SLOs. Deliverables include console UI changes, a short CS playbook, and an engineering runbook for rollback.
notes_to_self: Keep this contrarian framing when presenting: ask = what they say; leverage = what they actually need (predictability/cost). Prioritize low-friction probes first to build trust and reduce churn. Track any emergent asks in Slack thread linked above.
